note: Production S: one photoreal keyframe per V shot, made with FLUX.2 [dev] from the shot's Blender first frame (reference image 1: layout) and the approved character and prop sheets (images 2+). V animates from it (LTXVImgToVideoInplace), guided by the same plate, so the keyframe must keep the layout's geometry. All text is O's: signs, screens, mugs and the marquee stay blank here. A shot with "v" > 1 has a revised prompt: its files are <shot>_v<N>_s<seed>.png and log/prompts/keyframes/<shot>_v<N>.txt; earlier versions stay on disk. From v3 (2026-10-19) every frame starts from the VAE-encoded layout at partial denoise ("denoise"), so the geometry holds; the building sentence is chosen per shot from the layout's building_mask coverage ("building"), and the layout prefix bars extra people, crowds and crews. From v4 the layout prefix is positive only (negations about crowds and dogs added them), and every shot except the diner crowds (cast "patrons" in config/shots_b.json) gets the "empty" sentence. A shot may set its own "denoise" (v5: 0.96 where 0.92 kept stand-in blocks). v7 (2026-10-19, after [H] review): Blender source fixed (flag on its pole, pie and mug on a wider rail, cylindrical tank, leash hanging straight), layouts re-rendered; porch prompts name the clapboard siding, tower prompts the cylindrical tank. v8 (2026-10-19, agent review of v7): S04 names the bunting sign and the cranes, S13 the real corn, S27d the open fence and grass verge, S28a the whole massing as one church, S29, S29v and S33 the cornfield in front of the building; S05 and S31 keep v7 prompts with new seeds ("seeds"), S31 at 0.96. v9: S27d names the far gray box shapes as distant cows (v8 kept them as boxes). S31 and S31v v8 (2026-10-20, [H]): the layout's pie tin narrowed toward the top like a dog bowl; build_town.py now has a flared 9-inch tin with a lip and a domed pie, layouts re-rendered.
layout_prefix: Reference image 1 is a rough 3D layout of this exact shot. Keep its camera angle, lens, framing, horizon line and perspective exactly, and keep every building, object and figure in the same place, size and pose. Turn the gray stand-in shapes into the real, photographed things described below, as a still from a high-budget cinematic film.
style: Golden hour, low warm morning sun, cinematic 35mm film look, shallow depth of field, soft halation, warm color grade with neutral shadows. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing, no printing anywhere: every sign, screen, paper, gauge, label and mug is plain and blank.

S04.prompt: A wide, still morning landscape: flat green pasture with a wooden fence, black-and-white and brown dairy cows standing perfectly still, all facing the far horizon; a tall cornfield beyond, a silver water tower on steel legs, wooden power poles. On the far horizon, tiny with distance, the gray windowless building, exactly where it is in the layout. The water tower is a classic cylindrical silver steel tank with a conical roof, on four steel legs with diagonal cross-bracing. At the far left by the fence, a small plain white roadside sign board on two posts, completely blank, with red, white and blue pennant bunting along its lower edge. On the horizon behind the cornfield, three tall yellow construction tower cranes stand beside the tiny gray windowless building.

S05.prompt: The tall figure is the man from reference image 2 (same face, hair, red and black plaid flannel shirt, jeans), standing on the porch of a white clapboard farmhouse, smiling warmly, holding the plain white mug from reference image 4 near his chest. White painted porch posts and rail, dark shingled porch roof, a thin flagpole leaning out from the right post up out of frame.
